questions.stem:
How can teachers deal with children who are
non-attentive in the classroom?

options.text: Ask the children to go out of the class
Scold them frequently in front of the entire class
Talk to them and find out reasons for their disinterest
Given them a lot of worksheets as homework

questions.expected_answer: Talk to them and find out reasons for their disinterest
questions.supporting_excerpt:
How can teachers deal with children who are
non-attentive in the classroom? — Answer: Talk to them and find out reasons for their disinterest. If the teacher asks the non-attentive
children to go out the class then there will
be no learning opportunity. If they scolded
in front of the entire class, then it will affect
their self esteem. If lot of worksheets are
given as homework then they will be
demotivated.
Therefore, the best way is to talk to those
students so that the particular reason for
their disinterest can be identified.

questions.stem: The relationship between cognition and emotions is

options.text: independent of each other
uni-directional - emotions influence cognition
uni-directional - cognition influences emotions
bi-directional - a dynamic interplay between both

questions.expected_answer: bi-directional - a dynamic interplay between both
questions.supporting_excerpt:
The relationship between cognition and emotions is — Answer: bi-directional - a dynamic interplay between both. Cognition and emotion are dependant
variables, they are cause and effect of each
other. Emotion is a response of a cognitive
activity. Cognition in emotion is both a
necessary and a sufficient condition.
For example, thoughts are capable of
producing emotion and vice versa. Therefore
they are bi-directional means affect both ways.

(iii) Pedagogical strategies

to promote learning and memorizing.

Which of the following characterise the period of
‘middle childhood’?

options.text:
Physical growth and development occur at a very rapid
pace.

Ability to think abstractly and use of scientific reasoning
develops
Children begin to think logically but concretely

Learning occurs primarily through sensory and motor
activities

questions.expected_answer: Children begin to think logically but concretely
questions.supporting_excerpt:
Which of the following characterise the period of
‘middle childhood’? — Answer: Children begin to think logically but concretely. Middle childhood is a period from 6 to
12 years. During this stage, children begin to
thin logically about concrete events. Their
thinking become more logical and organised
but still very concrete.
13 
In this stage, children begin to experience
more of the world around them and try to
develop their own identity. In this stage,
children learn to adjust to school, with peers,
learn the culture and acquire new academic
skills.
